name: Queen mate
idea: Walk the lone king to the edge with the queen a knight's-move away, then bring your king up to mate. Watch for stalemate.

name: Rook mate
idea: Box the king with the rook, take the opposition with your king, then cut down a rank. The classic ladder mate.

name: Two-rook mate
idea: The lawnmower: rooks cut off ranks one after another, driving the king to the edge. Your own king isn't even needed.

name: Two-bishop mate
idea: Two bishops on adjacent diagonals build a wall. Push the king to a corner with the king's help to finish.

name: Bishop + knight mate
idea: The hardest basic mate. Drive the king to a corner the SAME colour as your bishop; the knight covers the escape. Mind the 50-move rule.

name: King in front on the sixth
idea: With your king ahead of the pawn on the sixth rank, it wins for any pawn but a rook pawn. Lead with the king, push the pawn last.

name: Connected passed pawns
idea: Two connected passers defend each other. Advance them side by side so the enemy king can never take one for free.

name: Hold with the opposition
idea: Defending in front of the pawn: step straight back and take the opposition when the enemy king advances. The pawn can't break through.

name: The rook-pawn draw
idea: Rook pawns are magic for the defender: reach the corner and shuffle there. With no room to outflank on the edge, it's a draw.

name: Lucena — building a bridge
idea: The most important winning rook ending. Put your rook on the fourth rank to build a bridge that shields your king from checks, then queen.

name: Philidor — third-rank defence
idea: Hold your rook on the sixth rank to keep the enemy king off it. The moment the pawn advances, switch to checking from behind.

name: Queen vs a pawn on the seventh
idea: Check, then hop the queen closer while the enemy king is forced in front of its own pawn. A centre pawn always loses — bring your king up.

name: The wrong bishop
idea: The bishop is the wrong colour for the a8 corner, so it can never control the queening square. Run your king to the corner and hold.

name: The king leads the pawn
idea: The king does the work, not the pawn. With your king two ranks ahead, take the opposition and outflank; only push the pawn once the king has cleared its path.

name: Réti's drawing king
idea: The famous save. Your king looks too far from either pawn — march it diagonally toward the corner so it threatens to catch the h-pawn AND shoulder your own c-pawn home. A drawn miracle.

name: Queen beats a knight's pawn
idea: Only rook and bishop pawns draw — a knight's pawn loses. Check to force the king in front of its pawn, use that free tempo to march your king closer, and repeat until you win it.

name: The right bishop and rook pawn
idea: Unlike the wrong bishop, this one guards the queening square. Because it covers a8 the enemy king can't blockade the corner, so just escort your rook pawn home.

name: Two knights can't mate
idea: Two knights cannot force mate against a lone king. Keep your king out of the corners and off the edge, give the knights nothing to trap, and the game is drawn.
